_about: The oil and gas timelapse (OilGasReplay.svelte, played by the shared Replay.svelte). Written by computer-scientist/article/oilgas/og_export.py from the record; do not edit by hand. Build input only.

boxes.label: Site camera: object on the pipe

frames.caption: An ordinary afternoon at the valve site. Flow in matches flow out.
Wave Pico doubts one pressure reading twice. A watch.
14:07. A truck drives in. No work order is on file.
Flow out falls behind flow in. Two records disagree. Flag.
A pressure reading goes flat. Wave Pico calls it stuck.
Wave Nano names the degraded sensor: upstream pressure.
The operator asks Wave Micro what changed. Simulated here.
14:55. The truck leaves. The gap starts to close.
The flag stays open. A person goes and looks.
Another day. A work order is on file for a valve test.
09:16. A truck drives in. The work order covers it.
The upstream sensor is out of service, as the work order says.
Both flows dip together. No gap between them.
The job ends. Nothing was flagged.

parts.name: Wave Nano
parts.role: on the mast: reads the sensors together

chat.q: What changed on this line since 14:00?
chat.a: A truck entered at 14:07 with no work order. Flow out fell behind flow in. One pressure reading went flat. Nothing here says who. Someone should go and look.

micro.rule: A flag is a question for a person. It never names anyone and never changes a bill.

note: The sensor readings and the gate and work-order entries are simulated, with the same sensor model our models are trained on. Wave Pico's and Wave Nano's answers are real: each was asked at every frame, read the way our benchmark reads them. The state is a site rule, not a model: a vehicle inside with no work order, a flow gap over the meters' tolerance, or the same sensor fault two frames running each count as one record out of line; one is a watch, two at once is a flag. Wave Micro is in training: its reply is a simulated example. The pictures are illustrations of no real site, and the boxes on them are the site camera system's own detections, simulated: no Wave model recognises a vehicle. A flag is a question for a person; it never names anyone and never changes a bill.
